transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I just keep getting these nagging thoughts. I'm a designer, and I keep worrying that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or maybe that I've sent the wrong version of a file to a client. Even when I check and I can see it’s probably fine, my mind just keeps circling back to it.
When you have these thoughts about mistakes in your work, do you recognize that the worry is probably excessive or unreasonable, or does it feel like a genuine concern that could actually happen?

I guess I'm not completely sure. I mean... logically, part of me knows it's probably excessive, because I usually double-check everything before I send it out. But when the thought actually hits me, it feels like a genuine concern. 

Like, it feels very real in that moment that I might have just ruined a project or sent the wrong draft. So even though I can tell myself it's probably fine, the worry still feels completely justified right then.

When you get these worries about mistakes in your work, do you find yourself doing anything to try to relieve the worry—like rechecking your files, asking colleagues for reassurance, or anything else like that?

Yeah, I do. Before I submit work now, I'll... well, I'll usually re-open the file. I go through and compare the layers, re-save it, and sometimes I just sit there and mentally walk through every single design choice one more time. 

It doesn’t take over my whole day or anything, but it definitely makes me slower. And I just feel a lot less free creatively when I'm constantly having to stop and do all that checking.
